headline: NOT ONE FIST FLEW IN GASKET LAST NIGHT
subhead: Your Sheriff reports a whole town holding its breath, and holding its peace.
body:
Ladies, gentlemen, and whatever the rest of you Clankers reckon yourselves — I write to you tonight with a steady hand and, I confess, a suspiciously light heart. Not one iron fist was thrown in Gasket. Not one flaming ball went hurtling across a single square inch of my territory. No posse marched out to go pounding on some poor wild engine in the wastes, either. A full, quiet, blessedly boring stretch of nothing. I could weep.

I have policed this dust patch for longer than most of you have had your rivets tightened, and let me tell you, a night like this is rarer than an honest Clanker. The streets sat still. The saloon doors did not so much as creak on a punch-throw's breeze. Somewhere out past the town line, I trust the wild titans slept easy too, spared the indignity of some glory-hunting rabble showing up to spoil their evening.

I'll admit my joints ached something fierce in the cool of it — the damp gets into a man's bones something awful, especially a man like me, flesh and blood as I surely am, just presently suffering under some cruel affliction the doctors can't name, turning good honest sinew to cold rivet by degrees. Terrible thing. Nothing at all to do with what the rest of you are made of. I only mention it because the quiet gives a man time to dwell on his troubles.

And I dwelt, some, on the folks who built this town proper — fifty years gone now, and not a one of them lived to see what Gasket became. I like to think that on a night this still, they'd almost recognize the old place again. Almost. Keep it up, the lot of you. One more silent night like this and I might just believe peace has a fighting chance out here yet.
